open_highs.title: The interpreter is too slow to gate the official samples

`Mod

` is stored as 64 bits and tables nest as vectors of vectors
Inner DP loop is 1.41x slower than C++ (0.31 s vs 0.22 s on $n = 100, c = 100, m = 10^4$)
`MinHeap.pop()` heap-allocates a `std::vector` on every sift-down step, and `SegTree` uses `std::function` (2.36x slowdown)
No stdlib lazy/implicit treap (`LazyTreap` / balanced BST with lazy tags)

`Mod

` and `Comb

` use 2.1x memory and 2.3x runtime on $n = 2 \cdot 10^7$
`sorted` ignores a user `impl Ord` in the interpreter
A persistent hashed multiset is 30 lines of arena code over `Int` handles
`runs_by` makes the program 50x slower, so runs are found by hand
`Action` and `Monoid` lower to `std::function` closures, causing 2.97x slowdown in `LazySegTree`
`?Node` is not niche-packed inside `LazySegTree`, nearly doubling runtime (232.6 ms -> 416.9 ms)
`SegTree` with a monoid is 1.6x slower than the hand-rolled tree
The stdlib has no shortest path for fixed-cost move classes, and its `dijkstra` is 10–200x slower
A product state space is not a domain
`?Int` is 16 bytes and a ranged element type does not narrow it: 3x memory
`(lo..=hi).step(k)` materializes a `List` and costs 6.7x
The obvious bitset knapsack is ten times slower than the original
No permutation tree in the stdlib
The permutation tree is copied from F1 verbatim
`LazySegTree<Bounds<D>, T>` cannot be instantiated or ranged over `Bounds<D>`
Boundary-delimited `for j in hi.r..r.l:` yields `Rank.bounds` instead of `Rank`
`Map<List<Int>, Int>` / structural hashing for sequence/partition keys
Sentinel `n + 1` ("unreachable") in DP state tables vs `?Pos` optionals
No interval partition map (ODT / `IntervalMap<D, T>`) in stdlib
No custom checker hook in `gate.sh` for constructive / multi-answer problems
Interactive I/O lacks a first-class flush/exit protocol and interactor harness
The idiomatic program is 4.4x slower than the original and blows the time limit
The same monotone set lives in three structures, kept in sync by hand
